claim_text: Antimony was detected in 12 of 24 wet-wipe nonwoven sheets, from 187.86 to 19,558.35 µg/L in the digest solution. The highest result is the rayon-only infant sheet (code ML). These figures are not milligrams per kilogram.
quote_trace: Table 5, unit µg/L; ML Sb 19,558.35±3,537.3, fiber Rayon. Abstract range 187.86±5.24 to 19,558.35±3,537.30 µg/L on 12 wet wipes.

claim_text: Nickel was detected in 2 of 24 wet-wipe sheets: 261.26±5.14 µg/L (rayon+polyester+cotton, infant) and 1,242.63±43.71 µg/L (United States, cloth-like). The other 22 sheets were not detected. Units are digest solution, not mg/kg.
quote_trace: Table 5 codes MO and PA*. Ni LOD 0.11 µg/L and LOQ 0.33 µg/L in Table 4.

claim_text: Cadmium, mercury, and thallium were not detected in any of the 24 wet-wipe sheets. Mercury was measured on a separate analyzer. The mercury quantification limit is 0.80 µg/L in Table 4 and 0.08 µg/L in the methods paragraph.
quote_trace: Table 5 dashes for Cd, Hg, and Tl on every wet-wipe row. Table 4 Hg LOQ 0.80. Methods: LOQ on arsenic, mercury and nickel is 007, 0.08, and 0.33 µg/L.

claim_text: A milligrams-per-kilogram reconstruction of the Choi digest was calculated and not adopted as the paper's result. The methods say the sample was diluted with 25 mL of water, not made up to 25 mL. If V is taken as 25 mL and mass as 0.200 g, mg/kg = C(µg/L) × 0.125. Code ML, rayon only, 19,558.35 µg/L, reconstructs to 2,444.79 mg/kg. If the 8 mL of acid is kept and 25 mL of water is added, the factor is 0.165 and the same sheet is 3,227.13 mg/kg. Mercury was not digested.
quote_trace: Section 2.2: Approximately 0.2 g of sample was added into a PTFE vessel containing 7 mL of 70% HNO3 and 1 mL of 50% HF. The samples were then transferred and diluted with 25 mL of ASTM type 1 water. Table 5 ML Sb 19,558.35 µg/L, fiber Rayon.

The results report says ICP-MS and cold-vapor atomic absorption and does not print 3052 or 6020. Printed wipe values below 1.0 ppm are not restated as less-than that plan limit.

claim_text: In a consumer-advocacy chart of single-unit ICP-MS tests, the nine baby-marked zinc oxide sunscreens had lead of 169.20 to 2,140.30 ppb and cadmium of 122.70 to 645.00 ppb as sold. Lead was reported above 5 ppb in 33 of 35 sunscreens and cadmium in 29 of 35; the two charted chemical-filter products were non-detect for lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic. Grey literature, one unit per product.

claim_text: A single-ingredient zinc oxide powder (100%) sold for making sunscreen had 9,474.70 ppb lead and 506.20 ppb cadmium in one unit, higher lead than any sunscreen on the same chart. Raw material, not a finished sunscreen.

claim_text: Five baby mineral sunscreen laboratory reports (cases 2507165, 2505470, 2506212, 2505271, 2505468) give lead of 169.2, 330.0, 495.1, 1017.5 and 1251.1 ppb and cadmium of 166.1, 218.6, 232.4, 356.1 and 575.5 ppb as sold; total arsenic 485.3 and 135.9 ppb in two, below 10 ppb in three; mercury below 5 ppb in all. Values read from the report images; OCR text layers were wrong in three reports.

A 2026 company screening of 35 retail sunscreens (one unit each, ICP-MS after AOAC 2015.01 digestion, LOQ 0.004 mg/kg) quantified lead in all 35 (0.006 to 4.960 mg/kg) and cadmium in 21 (0.005 to 0.603 mg/kg). Every cadmium-quantified unit had lead of at least 0.125 mg/kg and every cadmium-ND unit at most 0.079 mg/kg; median lead 0.620 versus 0.0165 mg/kg. The four units named mineral were all cadmium-positive. Digestion recovery from mineral particles was not evaluated.

Numeric profiles: lead 0.3 and 0.8 mg/kg (two pigmentary grades) and 3 mg/kg (one nano grade). Arsenic, cadmium, lead and antimony are 0.5 N HCl-extractable, not total.

claim_text: EU Annex VI (point-in-time 31 December 2020) permits titanium dioxide and zinc oxide at up to 25 % each and sets purity conditions for the nano forms (TiO2 ≥ 99 %; ZnO ≥ 96 % with non-CO2, non-water impurities below 1 % in total) but no element-specific lead, cadmium, arsenic or mercury limit. The SCCS nano zinc oxide (2012) and nano titanium dioxide (2014) opinions record that no analytical impurity data were submitted.

claim_text: In Canada, sunscreens with only titanium dioxide and zinc oxide (each up to 25 %) are natural health products whose finished-product specifications follow the NNHPD Quality Guide, which sets topical limits of 3 ppm arsenic, 3 ppm cadmium, 10 ppm lead, 1 ppm total mercury and 5 ppm antimony. A topical chromium value in the guide's appendix conflicts with its body table and species label and is not used.

claim_text: On intact adult skin, zinc oxide nanoparticles stayed on the surface or in the stratum corneum while zinc ions reached the viable epidermis (exogenous 1.0 ± 0.3 µg/mL versus endogenous 4.3 ± 0.7 µg/mL, ex vivo); tracer zinc in blood after five days of outdoor use was about one thousandth of total blood zinc. No study in this collection measured lead, cadmium, arsenic or mercury crossing skin from a sunscreen, and none used infant skin.
